Web design in East Texas is a different job from web design in Dallas. The customers are spread across pine country, small county seats and two mid-size metros, Tyler and Longview, and a good share of them are driving in from somewhere else. Dominion Web Design Pro is based right in the middle of that, in Big Sandy in Upshur County, and builds sites for the businesses that serve it: every page written by hand by Maurice Johnson, with a free demo before you pay anything.

East Texas web design for a region, not a single city

Texas Parks and Wildlife describes the Pineywoods as an ecoregion reaching into parts of about 40 counties along the state's eastern edge, running up against Louisiana and Arkansas, and most of its land is timberland. That shapes the economy as much as the scenery: sawmills and timber haulers, poultry and cattle, oil and gas service, and the welders, mechanics and contractors who keep all of it running.

It also shapes how people search. Someone in Ore City or Hallsville may drive half an hour to buy a part, see a specialist or get a truck fixed, so they look up the business before they leave home. If the only thing online is a Facebook page with old hours, they pick whoever looks open. That is the gap a plain, honest, fast website closes, and it is a gap almost every small town here still has.

What an East Texas business website has to do

Out here, a website rarely has to impress anyone. It has to answer four questions fast, on a phone with one bar of signal: what do you do, do you come out to my town, are you open, and how do I reach you. Plenty of small business sites around the region miss at least one of those.

  • Say the towns out loud. If you serve Big Sandy, Hawkins and Mineola, the site should say so, in words, on pages written for those places.
  • Put the phone number where a thumb can reach it. Tap to call at the top of every page, and the same number your truck and your Facebook page show.
  • Keep the hours honest. Seasonal hours, hunting season closures, festival weekends: if they change, the site should change with them.
  • Load quickly on a weak signal. Pages built light, photos sized properly, nothing that makes a visitor wait.
  • Belong to you. Your domain in your name, a one-time price, and no platform that takes the site away if you stop paying.

Every package covers those basics. Starter is $497 for five pages. Pro is $997 and adds 10 city pages, which is usually the right fit for a contractor or service business covering a couple of counties. Agency is $1,997 and starts with keyword research across your whole territory, then builds a page for every town and service combination worth having. All three are one-time prices; the pricing page lists every detail, including the optional AI agents.

Metro or small town: two different jobs

In Tyler and Longview

You are competing. A search for a dentist, a roofer or a lawyer in either city brings back a full page of businesses, several of them with decent sites and a pile of reviews. What separates you there is specific copy: the neighborhoods you work in, the services you actually offer listed one by one, real photos of your crew and your shop, and a page for each service instead of one long list. That is where the Pro and Agency packages earn their price.

In the smaller towns

You are often the only one. In a town of a few thousand, the plumber or the cafe with a working website and a filled-in map listing is frequently the only result that looks open. The job is less about outranking anyone and more about simply existing online, accurately. A five-page Starter site does that well, and it is the first thing we would suggest for most single-location businesses in places like Gilmer, Gladewater or Big Sandy.

Many East Texas businesses live in both worlds at once: a contractor based in Kilgore who takes jobs in Longview, or a Gilmer shop that wants Tyler customers to make the drive. For them the answer is usually a solid main site plus city pages for the bigger towns they reach into, each one written for that town.

Free business help across the region

East Texas has two Small Business Development Centers that give free advising, and most owners have never called either one.

UT Tyler-Longview SBDC

Covers Gregg, Harrison, Marion, Panola, Rusk and Upshur counties, with offices in Longview, Marshall, Jefferson and Henderson. Named the SBA's 2024 SBDC of the Year for the North Texas region.

Tyler SBDC at Tyler Junior College

Covers Smith, Cherokee, Wood, Nacogdoches, Sabine, San Augustine and Shelby counties from its office at the college in Tyler.

Local chambers of commerce in Tyler, Longview, Kilgore, Marshall, Gilmer and Gladewater round out the list. We have no arrangement with any of them; they are simply good first calls.

Straight answer on location: Dominion Web Design Pro has no office in Tyler, Longview or the other towns on this page. Maurice Johnson builds every site from Big Sandy in East Texas and delivers it remotely, by link, phone and email.

Common questions

Is there a web designer in East Texas who works with small towns?

Yes. Dominion Web Design Pro is based in Big Sandy, in Upshur County, and many businesses around here are in towns of a few thousand people. A site for a Gilmer feed store or a Gladewater antique dealer gets the same hand-written pages as one for a Tyler clinic.

How much does East Texas web design cost?

Three one-time prices: $497 for a 5-page Starter site, $997 for Pro with 10 pages and 10 city pages, and $1,997 for Agency, which starts with keyword research across your whole service area. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep the AI agent.

My customers are spread across three or four East Texas counties. How should my website handle that?

With one page per town that is worth having, each written for that town. The Pro package includes 10 city pages, and the Agency package covers every town-and-service combination the research says people search for. A single page that lists twenty town names does very little. See how city pages work.

Do small East Texas towns even search for businesses online?

They do, and more than most owners expect, because so many customers are driving in from somewhere else: a festival weekend, a hospital visit in Tyler, a job at a Longview plant, an antique run to Gladewater. Those people have no neighbor to ask. They search.

Can I meet the person building my website if I am in East Texas?

You can certainly talk to him. Maurice is the one who calls you back, and Big Sandy is within driving distance of most of the region. Most of the work is still done by link, phone and email, since that keeps it moving. Call (903) 636-7511; the AI receptionist can put you through to Maurice.

Run a business in East Texas? See your site first.

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
